title: Kingdom of Prussia
capsule: The Kingdom of Prussia was proclaimed on 18 January 1701 when Elector Frederick III of Brandenburg crowned himself Frederick I, having secured imperial permission to use the royal title for his territories outside the Holy Roman Empire. Under Frederick the Great (r. 1740–1786) Prussia seized Silesia from Austria in the War of the Austrian Succession, fought off a coalition of France, Austria, and Russia in the Seven Years' War (1756–1763), and emerged as a great power. After leading the unification of Germany through wars against Denmark (1864), Austria (1866), and France (1870–71), Prussia became the dominant state within the German Empire proclaimed in 1871, retaining its constitutional identity until the abolition of German monarchies in 1918.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Prussian borders are among the best-documented in early modern European history, with detailed treaty boundaries; the dataset's truncation at 1864 reflects political rather than territorial ambiguity.
